stem: A provider orders an amikacin trough concentration. When should the serum specimen be collected?

options.A: Collect the specimen shortly after the dose is given, using the post-dose concentration as the trough value.
options.B: Collect the specimen near the midpoint of the dosing interval, before serum concentrations reach the end-of-interval level.
options.C: Collect the specimen immediately before the next scheduled dose so it represents the trough concentration.
options.D: Wait until the amikacin course is finished, then collect the specimen after no further doses are scheduled.

rationale: Current Mayo Clinic Laboratories ordering guidance states that an amikacin trough specimen should be collected immediately before the next scheduled dose. The same page distinguishes this from a peak specimen, which is collected 30–60 minutes after the last dose. Therefore C is correct. A describes a post-dose/peak context, B is not trough timing, and D would not provide therapeutic trough monitoring during treatment.
educational_objective: Collect an amikacin trough specimen immediately before the next scheduled dose so the measured concentration represents the end of the dosing interval.
source_document_title: RAMIK — Amikacin, Random, Serum; ordering guidance for TAMIK trough

source_locator: Ordering Guidance: peak specimen 30–60 minutes after last dose; trough specimen immediately before next scheduled dose; order TAMIK / Amikacin, Trough, Serum.

correction_summary: Removed distractor-only 'only' wording and made all options plausible specimen-timing choices while preserving Mayo's exact trough timing.

audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: PASS — Mayo explicitly distinguishes trough immediately before next dose from peak 30–60 minutes post-dose.
